acceptance: Workflow unit tests cover: certified SHA skips fast-test and medium-test; uncertified SHA, API failure, non-success queue run, wrong workflow path, and ci-required-result not success all run the full gates.
The lint job and the fast-lane count cache write still run on every develop push.
Auto-revert-on-failure cannot trigger from a certified skip, proven by a test; green-run-cleanup and metrics record the certifying run ID.
Browser develop-push runs apply the same certification rule, including the browser gate check.
After landing, the first 10 develop merges show certified skips with the correct run IDs in the step summary, and any merge without a successful queue run executes the full gates.
Post-landing note reports measured runner-minutes saved on those merges against the ~40 min per push baseline.
context:
Guardrails (all mandatory):
1. Certified means ALL of: a workflow run with event `merge_group`, path `.github/workflows/pr.yml`, conclusion `success`, `head_sha` exactly equal to `github.sha`, and its `ci-required-result` job concluded `success`. For the browser workflow, also require that run's `Results Explorer browser gate` success on the same SHA. Nothing else counts: no tree matching, no PR-run evidence, no parent inheritance.
2. Fail open. Any API error, pagination gap, missing permission, ambiguous match, or timeout runs the full gates. Log the reason in the step summary.
3. Keep the `lint` job running unchanged. It writes the `fast-lane-count-develop-<sha>` cache that the PR `guard-fast-lane-delta` step restores. Skipping it would silently break that guard.
4. `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` never use the skip. `workflow_dispatch` stays the manual escape hatch for a full run.
5. Auto-revert must never fire on a certified skip. `green-run-cleanup`, `metrics`, and the post-merge signature pipeline must treat a certified skip as an explicit third state ("certified by run N"). It is never a failure and never a fresh green baseline that clears an unrelated open incident. Read the signature and EXPECTED_SIGNATURE_JOBS code before choosing the representation.
6. Grant only `actions: read` to the lookup job.
7. No change to pr.yml, required checks, or ruleset 15611785.
description:
The native merge queue fast-forwards develop to the exact commit it tested. `develop-post-merge.yml` then runs lint, fast-test, and medium-test again on that same SHA. The results-explorer browser workflow does the same on develop push.

Evidence (native-queue era, 2026-08-23 to 2026-09-16):
- 77 of the last 80 develop commits equal the head SHA of a successful `merge_group` run of `.github/workflows/pr.yml`.
- 240 of 262 post-merge push runs were on such queue-certified SHAs.
- All 8 post-merge push failures (all `fast-test`) were on queue-certified SHAs. They were nondeterministic failures (a seed-drift test and an xdist worker crash), not regressions. Auto-revert PRs #2020, #2068, and #2073 in the same window were all closed unmerged.
- Sampled push runs spend about 40 runner-minutes on fast-test plus medium-test (fast 17-22 min, medium 11-22 min). Develop-push browser runs used about 1,700 runner-minutes in the window.

Change: add a certification lookup at the start of `develop-post-merge.yml` push runs, and of `results-explorer-browser.yml` develop push runs. When the pushed SHA is queue-certified, skip fast-test and medium-test (and the browser suite) and record the certifying run ID. Every other path runs as today.

This item changes no required check, no ruleset setting, and no pr.yml job.
